lines: POSTMASTER: Storm took the road out.
The last cable car leaves at dusk.
Three letters must go up the mountain
today. Will you carry the bag?
POSTMASTER: Farm, mine, lighthouse.
Don't miss a single one.
POSTMASTER: Farm east, mine west, and the
lighthouse beyond the pine trail.
POSTMASTER: Dusk won't wait, courier.
KEEPER: Matches, hot soup, stamps —
everything a mountain route needs.
KEEPER: Dry tinder meets its match.
KEEPER: Five gold, friend. The chest
up north has loose coin, they say.
KEEPER: Still steaming. For the miner?
He has not left his hut in days.
KEEPER: Fifteen gold a bowl. The rain
makes every copper feel farther.
KEEPER: First-class ink, mountain-grade.
KEEPER: Stamps cost ten. The east farm
pays well for a hand with sheep.
KEEPER: Two woodland mushrooms, six gold.
A fair price on a wet day.
KEEPER: One mushroom, three gold. The
pine trail grows more by the minute.
KEEPER: Bring pine-trail mushrooms and
I will buy them, three gold each.
CLERK: Five of my parcels blew across
the mountain. I would pay twenty gold
for all five.
CLERK: The route is safer with you on it.
CLERK: All five! Here is twenty gold,
and my thanks. Rain or shine, courier.
CLERK: Check the farm, mine, pine trail,
and the lighthouse path. Wind travels.
Found 25 gold saved for cable repairs.
The mountain can have it, for today.
Empty now. The rain drums the lid like
a counter waiting for coin.
<Mountain Hamlet>
E: East-Slope Farm   W: West Mine
N: Pine Trail -> Lighthouse
Out of service — the road is out.
All mail goes by hand up the trail.
<Cable Car Station>
Last car today: dusk. After that,
the mountain walks alone.
FARMER: The east bridge holds, mostly.
Mind the sheep. They have opinions.
FARMER: A letter? Aye — but first,
three hay bundles from the field edge,
or the sheep won't follow me home.

FARMER: Three dry bundles, by the field
edge. Rain swells the rest.
FARMER: They will wait. Hay won't.
FARMER: Post's business, is it? I'll take
my letter once the sheep are settled.
FARMER: Sheep are quiet, letter is read.
Safe on the rocks up high.

MINER: That fever... the rain bit deep.
Hot soup would put me right. The
general store keeps it simmering.
MINER: Steam right to the bones. Here,
your letter — stamped and read. Go,
the trail worsens past the pines.
MINER: Soup from the hamlet store.
Fifteen gold, worth every copper.
MINER: I'll be here. The mountain
is in no hurry today.
MINER: Post can wait till my hands stop
shaking. Soup first, letters after.
MINER: Warm again. The pine bridge is
out, you know. The hermit can help.
The apothecary's window is shuttered.
A chalk note: SOUP, HOT, OFTEN.
<West-Slope Mine>
The ore waits. The fever doesn't.
A parcel wedged behind the cart
rails. Into the bag it goes.
HERMIT: Bridge north is out. I can cut
new planks, but my tinder is soaked.
One box of matches and I'll work.
HERMIT: Smoke, then flame. Listen —
planks already falling into place.
The lighthouse road is yours.
HERMIT: The hamlet store sells them,
five gold the box.
HERMIT: Rain waits. The bridge waits.
HERMIT: Cross anywhere on the planks.
Tell the keeper the mountain still
remembers its lights.
Cold ash and wet kindling.
The fire pops, dry and warm. Somewhere
north, new planks settle on the bridge.
Picked woodland mushrooms. The shop
buys these on wet days.

A parcel hung on a low pine bough.
The bag is getting full.
A loose plank rattles over the gap.
You kick it into place.
The bridge is gone — wet timber and air
between here and the lighthouse.
KEEPER: You are late. The beam must
turn before the cable car stops.
KEEPER: My letter, in the rain. Light
the three lamps by the tower, then
the door will open.
KEEPER: No time for visitors. Post first.
KEEPER: Three lamps. They burn on their
own once they catch.

THE END.
The beam cuts the storm open. Three
letters delivered to the mountain.
The last car of the day carries the
courier down, and the rain lightens.
The last parcel, at the top of the
world. The clerk will not believe it.
